//: Story Phase 5, chapter 22: The Grand Stenchmaster's Office. Noon. The station midships is now officially his (stenchmaster_station_unlocked): the S.E.S. (14,17), his grog table (13,17), his chair (14,18), the Forecast Board (10,16), the Stench Log (12,16), the crayons (13,16). A real Shark Duty shift (office_watch, both rails, a boarder) while Garrick heckles from his chair; the rudder; the Stench Log; the chair, while he's off doing 'quality assurance' in the galley; three crew complaints; optional Center vignettes (fresh bread in the galley, 'I'll wait.' at the washroom). Then Pete's rope, three bells, the Center sits on the station, the laundry goes yellow, Ned takes the long way round, and Garrick comes back and sits in it.

p5c3.begin.narrate: The sharks had not gone away. They had simply rearranged themselves into a queue.

p5c3.begin: jory[determined]: Both rails this time, Captain! They've worked out there's two sides to a boat.
jory: And mind the deck. The big ones have started coming ABOARD.
Behind you, very faintly, a man argues with a turnip.

p5c3.begin.tutorial: Shark Duty: hold both rails and heave any boarders back over. The Grand Stenchmaster will be... supervising.
p5c3.begin.title: The Grand Stenchmaster's Office

p5c3.duty_done: The last shark of the shift slides away, looking wounded in its feelings. The crew collapse against the rail.

p5c3.duty_done.text: Wonderful work, everyone! I've written it down!

p5c3.duty_done.say: nell[concerned]: Captain! The wheel's shuddering! Something's at the rudder!
p5c3.duty_done.name: Nell (from the helm)

p5c3.duty_done.tutorial: Check the rudder: take the wheel on the quarterdeck (aft, past the cabin).
p5c3.duty_done.title: The Grand Stenchmaster's Office

p5c3.rudder: You take the wheel. It fights you like a dog on a lead. Down below the stern, something is chewing.
nell[annoyed]: It's the same one, Captain. Big grey fella with a notch in his fin. I've named him Admiral.
nell[smug]: He's eating the ship from the back and doesn't care who knows it.
You'll need the crew on it. You take a breath and do the thing captains are for.

then: Rook runs aft with a boathook and leans over the taffrail, jabbing downward and making a noise like an offended goose.

choice.text: "Pete! Sully! Bucket of bilge on the rudder!"
then: Pete and Sully haul a bucket of bilge water to the stern and tip it over. A moment later, Admiral surfaces, gags, and swims off to reconsider.
He does not get up. He points, regally, at Rook. Rook goes, because somebody has to, swearing every step of the way.
rook[annoyed]: He DELEGATED me. Nobody gave him delegating!

p5c3.rudder: There's a splash, a swirl, and the wheel stops shuddering. Admiral has gone to sulk somewhere off the port quarter.
nell: Thank you, Captain. She steers. Mostly. There's a dent in the rudder the shape of his opinion.

p5c3.rudder.tutorial: Have a proper look at the Grand Stenchmaster's 'office'. Start with the Stench Log (on its stand at his station).
p5c3.rudder.title: The Grand Stenchmaster's Office

p5c3.log: The Stench Log lies open on its stand. Somebody has been sleeping on it.
A large, damp, roughly face-shaped patch covers most of the right-hand page. In the margin, in very small crayon: ADMINISTRATIVE MOISTURE.
Under 'MORNING' it says MONITORED READINESS. That's all. That's the whole morning.
captain[disgusted]: He wrote down that he was ready. He spent the morning being ready, and then he wrote it down.

p5c3.log.text: It's a very thorough log, Captain.

p5c3.log: garrick[businesslike]: Excuse me, Captain. If you'll mind the office. I must conduct the noon Frog Grog quality assurance.
He walks off to the main hatch with his mug, humming the national anthem of a country that doesn't exist.
And for the first time all day, the chair is empty.

p5c3.log.tutorial: The chair is empty. Inspect the Grand Stenchmaster's chair.
p5c3.log.title: The Grand Stenchmaster's Office

p5c3.chair: The Grand Stenchmaster's chair: a barrel with a cushion on it, a hatch cover upholstered with what used to be your cabin curtain, and a mustard throw over one arm.
You put a hand on the seat.
captain[resigned]: I hate that he was telling the truth.

then: You sit down in the Grand Stenchmaster's chair.
You stand up immediately, and look round to see if anyone saw. Everyone saw.

p5c3.chair.tutorial: Hear the crew's complaints. (Anyone will do. Everyone has some.)
p5c3.chair.title: The Grand Stenchmaster's Office

p5c3.qa: The Grand Stenchmaster stands at the Frog Grog cask with his little finger out, swilling a mouthful round his teeth like a wine merchant.
garrick[businesslike]: Today's batch: notes of pond. Notes of ink. A finish of... regret. Long finish. Very long finish.
garrick[proud]: I'd give it a seven.
mags[angry]: He's been 'assuring' it for twenty minutes. There's a ring round the cask where he's lowered it.
garrick[smug]: Quality takes time, Mistress Mags.
p5c3.bread: Salty Jim is easing a tray of bread out of the oven. Proper bread. Golden. It smells of bread, and only a little of everything else.
jim[happy]: Look at that, Captain. First proper loaf in a week. I've been nursing that dough like a baby.
The Dead Center pours down it, rolls across the stove and settles, with a contented sort of slump, right on top of the bread.
Jim does not scream. Jim does not move. Jim stares into the middle distance, at something about a thousand miles away.
He puts down the oven cloth, very gently, and walks out of the galley without a word.
mags[concerned]: Give him a minute, Captain. He named the dough.
p5c3.washroom: Brask is standing by the washroom door with a towel over his shoulder and a toothbrush in his teeth. His turn.
A warm yellow light spills out over his boots. Something inside the washroom shifts, the way a bear shifts in a cave.
He closes the door again, quietly, and stands there.
brask[laugh]: Don't look at me like that, Captain. It was in there FIRST.
p5c3.station: Pete is up a ratline at the mainmast, splicing a chewed rope, tongue between his teeth.
A thin yellow tendril curls up over the starboard rail. It sniffs the air, if a cloud can sniff, and comes on deck.
It rolls straight over the washing line. Every shirt on it turns the colour of old custard, all at once, like a flag going up.

p5c3.station.tutorial: Three bells! The Center is on the station. Get clear: aft by the cabin door, or forward by the foremast.
p5c3.station.title: The Grand Stenchmaster's Office

p5c3.station_clear: From a safe distance, the crew watch the Dead Center settle over the Grand Stenchmaster's station: the chair, the grog table, the Forecast Board, the S.E.S. The screen glows through it, faintly green, like a lamp in fog.
It's still playing. Through all of it, it's still playing.
Ned comes up the fore hatch with an armful of charts for the helm, sees the cloud between him and the quarterdeck, and stops.
He turns round and goes back down the fore hatch.
Some time later, he comes out of the cabin door behind you, holding the same charts, with cobwebs in his hair and one boot wet.
ned[disgusted]: Crew quarters. Galley. Hold. Bilge. Back up through the hold. Through the GALLEY again. And your cabin, Captain, sorry about the window.
And up out of the main hatch, right into the middle of the cloud, comes the Grand Stenchmaster with a fresh mug of Frog Grog.
He does not stop. He does not cough. He strolls through the Dead Center like a man walking through a light drizzle, and settles into his chair.
gristle[disgusted]: That's the worst part. That's the worst part of the whole thing.
After a while the Center gets bored, as it always does, and drifts off over the side. It leaves the station exactly as it found it, only slightly more so.

p5c3.station_clear.text: The chair has never been warmer, Captain!
